spacertales-misfiled-can.title: A can in the wrong column
spacertales-misfiled-can.notes: Original correspondence, not a native plot. One run per save; dismissing its goal sets it aside. Agent-selected homes and cast are in this file's people and threads tables. Letters begin here after the required news or file is known. An existing docking at the arc's place counts; the correspondence may continue after departure. No money or existing goods are taken or granted. Completion gives one data card. Waiting advances correspondence, not machine work. No standing change is proposed. No owns gate: the can is checked only when carried, by the example step. The offer does not claim a can is aboard.

objective.title: Wait for the freight note
objective.description: Give the receiving clerk at [place] an hour to check the old freight description.

message.text: [player-first], I keep the receiving file at [place]. The notice concerned the Sable Margin: two contractors claim the same old shipment, and its crew sent a third account. I'd like to compare the cargo description with a current D20. I'm checking the note first. The example will stay yours.
The note says service records where it should name what the cans hold. A clerk copied a heading into the cargo column. I'd like to compare a real can before circulating the correction.

objective.title: Bring a Rivetline D20 to [place]
objective.description: Be at [place] with a Phobos' Rivetline D20 Drain Canister on you (a bag counts), so the clerk can compare it with the old description. You keep the can and what is in it.

message.text: Bring a D20 into the comparison while you are at [place], where this receiving account is kept. Being here already counts. Nobody is taking the can. It helps identify a product description, not decide who owned the old shipment.
Comparison noted. Process contents, not office records. I'll separate that correction from the ownership claims. The Sable Margin's crew have asked for their names to stay with the repair letters.

objective.title: Wait for the corrected freight account
objective.description: Give the clerk two hours to send the corrected account round. Your copy comes on a data card.

message.text: One contractor wants the corrected heading but not the crew's covering letter. The other wants its own name on both. I'm sending the correction with an explanation of what it does and doesn't prove.

Sent. The account can now describe a can without deciding whose it was. Small result, I know. The crew have had larger claims disappear into smaller mistakes than this. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Bring an aluminium ingot to [place]
objective.description: Be at [place] with one Rivetline Aluminium Ingot on you (a bag counts). Bought, found or made, any ingot will do, and you keep it.

message.text: The freight copy you opened mentions an ingot entered as a spare assembly. I keep the comparison at [place]. A current Rivetline aluminium ingot would help read that line. Bought, found or made is fine. Keep it. The workers' letters need a different kind of evidence.
Right description, wrong claim. The broker wants to use your example as proof of the old job. It can't prove that. The workers' signed repair letters are separate evidence.

objective.title: Wait for the workers' letters to be attached
objective.description: Give the clerk three hours to attach the workers' old repair letters to the material description.

message.text: The letters name the people who kept the equipment working while the replacement shipment was late. One contractor wants the dates. Neither asked for the names. I'm keeping both.

Addendum sent. It says what your sample established, then reproduces the workers' account separately. No verdict, no recovered wages. At least nobody can claim the names weren't supplied. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

spacertales-meal-in-the-margin.notes: Original correspondence, not a native plot. One run per save; dismissing its goal sets it aside. objective.title: Wait for Verdemorrow's galley letter
objective.description: Give the archivist an hour to look into the old galley photograph.

message.text: [person:spacertales-neri-vale] sent the freight copy you opened to our Verdemorrow archive. I keep the galley correspondence; the comparison is being filed at [place]. The Sable Margin photograph credits a contractor's provision programme. The crew's letter credits people. I'll find the caption.
The crew account names a grower, a cook and the installer still owed a meal. The photograph has the contractor's logo on a borrowed jacket. Both describe the same supper.

objective.title: Bring Verdemorrow lettuce to [place]
objective.description: Be at [place] with one Verdemorrow Lettuce portion on you (a bag counts), for the archive's comparison. Bought, found or grown, any will do, and you keep it.

message.text: One lettuce portion while you are at [place] will do for the present-day entry. It stays with you. The old photograph needs the names in its own letter; your example mustn't be mistaken for evidence of that crop.
Example recorded separately. No yield claims, no claim that your rack grew it. Now we can caption the old photograph with the names in the letter.

objective.title: Wait for the crew names to join the photograph
objective.description: Give the archivist two hours to write the new caption with the crew's names.

message.text: The contractor calls the new caption a distraction from its provision programme. The cook's letter calls supper a distraction from the contractor. We have enough room for the crew names.

Names added. The meal's gone, the ship has another name, and someone still owes the installer supper. We'll keep the old invoice with the photograph. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Wait for Asterel's old service letter
objective.description: Give the Asterel service desk two hours to find the record under the board's old plate number.

message.text: I work on Asterel service files at [place]. [person:spacertales-neri-vale] forwarded the freight correspondence you opened. It mentions one of our boards, recorded as replacement pending. I'm looking under the plate number. This is an old covering letter, not a fault report for your module.
Found the letter under the plate number, not the ship name. The watchkeeper wrote down which repair got the board back into service. The contractor recorded replacement pending.

objective.title: Acknowledge Asterel at [place]
objective.description: Be at [place] so the service reply joins the receiving account. If you are already there, that counts.

message.text: Acknowledgement at [place] will keep the copy with the receiving account that introduced it. You are not testing a board or accepting an old warranty. Being here already is enough for this correspondence.

Acknowledged. Useful repair, accurately described. Somebody called the board Tomorrow in the margin. I hope its next owner kept the name. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Wait for the four makers' leaflets
objective.description: Give the broker two hours to gather what each maker says about the proposed plant.

message.text: [player-first], the mixed-plant questions on the news came through our trade desks at [place]. I have four makers' leaflets for one proposed bill. As a V4 owner, you know a machine is only part of a job. I'm checking whether anyone described the joins.
Nobody did. Each list ends where the next begins. Fennmark named stores, Tolvane named its outputs, Lixivar named feed, Oxsmith named heat. That's information, not yet a whole quotation.

objective.title: Return the quotation at [place]
objective.description: Be at [place] so the broker can send the incomplete quotation back for revision. If you are already there, that counts.

message.text: I'll return the bill through the desk at [place] with the original questions attached. Being here closes this part of the correspondence. Don't buy another machine for it. Four accurate makers' names aren't a connection.
Returned. They offered matching enamel instead. I asked again for the equipment around the equipment. No agreement yet. That's the honest answer.

objective.title: Wait for the broker's final note
objective.description: Give the broker four hours to write back.

message.text: The customer has paused the order. Suppliers want to know which of them lost the sale. The answer seems to be the space between them.

File closed with no order. We kept the useful descriptions and declined the incomplete bill. Sometimes a ship's best new equipment is the equipment it hasn't bought yet. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Bring Alembrine spirit to [place]
objective.description: Be at [place] with one bottle of Alembrine Spirit on you (a bag counts), so the desk can compare it with the old letters. Any bottle will do, and you keep it.

message.text: I keep Alembrine customer letters at [place], the desk in the label notice. We have two old accounts involving a bottle and a borrowed pump. A current bottle can help check the product description. Carry one here if you can. It stays yours; nobody is asking you to brew or find a pump.
Description noted. The bottle in the story was ordinary stock, not some special commission. Now to find out whether it settled the quarrel or went to the wrong ship.

objective.title: Wait for the two pump accounts
objective.description: Give the old customers three hours to reply about the borrowed pump.

message.text: First reply says the bottle arrived at the intended ship and improved relations. Second says the intended ship had already changed owners. Both say the pump remained somebody else's problem.

We can't reconcile the accounts. We'll retain both and label the uncertainty. If a dealer promises the bottle fixed the pump dispute, they're selling a better ending than we have. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Wait for Halewright's fitting letter
objective.description: Give Halewright half an hour to send the fitting letter.

message.text: I keep the Halewright fitting archive at [place], where the notice came from. Ward-3 owners may recognise the Short Return letters: a bed, a crowded loading plan and a crew reply. I'll send them as fitting history. There is no patient to examine and no test of your sickbay.
The first letter lists cargo that would no longer fit. The reply lists people who might need the bed. Both lists were written by the same crew member.

objective.title: Wait for the Short Return watch letter
objective.description: Give Halewright two hours to find the watchkeeper's letter.

message.text: The equipment account says bed and monitor supplied. A watchkeeper asked us to keep another account with it. I'm looking for the copy. There's no clinical record here, and we won't invent one.
Found it. Names, watch times and treatment supplies brought to the bed. It doesn't say which machine saved anyone. It says the people expected back reached dock.

objective.title: Acknowledge the watch at [place]
objective.description: Be at [place], where Halewright keeps this correspondence, to close it. If you are already there, that counts.

message.text: The watch letter will stay beside the fitting notes here at [place]. Being here is enough to close your copy of the correspondence. You owe no case report, and you need not put anyone in a bed.

Acknowledged. The equipment had its invoice. The watch now has its names. Leave room for another person. In the fitting notes that sentence is still literal. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Wait for the disputed drawing account
objective.description: Give it an hour for the account of the old refit dispute to arrive.

message.text: You opened the freight copy. I have another ledger account now, sent through [place]: a crew's old sales drawing and a newer one showing its refits. The contractor preferred the clean old sheet. I'm finding the crew's reply. These are historical letters, not schematics for [ship].
The reply says the drawing was accurate once. Someone crossed out once and wrote before we lived here. It's the clearest distinction in the file.

objective.title: Close the drawing file at [place]
objective.description: Be at [place], where the crew's drawing account was sent. If you are already there, that counts.

message.text: The file has drawings and arguments, not a schematic for [ship]. The copy closes at [place], where the crew sent it. You don't need to suffer damage or change your repair plans. Being here already counts.

Copy acknowledged. The old drawing stayed in the file with the newer one. A ship can keep its history without rebuilding itself to match it. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.

objective.title: Wait for Slingwright's photograph dispute
objective.description: Give the worker an hour to send their account of the photograph.

message.text: I handle Slingwright customer letters at [place]. The notice concerned a worker's account of an RM-1 publicity photograph. The empty plant was credited to the feeder; the loading was done by a person. I'm finding the signed letter for operators who want the whole description.
The letter says the feeder had a supported job, but the worker supplied the lifting. The fee bought a photograph, not a shift of loading. Sales had filed it under image corrections.

objective.title: Wait for the caption and the fee to be separated
objective.description: Give Slingwright two more hours to close the correspondence.

message.text: We'll separate the accurate equipment claim from the worker's unpaid-work claim. One doesn't settle the other. You don't need to run a batch to help us read the letter.

File corrected. The machine did its job with supplied feed. A person supplied that feed. The fee dispute is still a fee dispute; the corrected photograph no longer makes the person disappear. A data card holds the retained account; open it on a computer or PDA.
